## Ingest
Quick review of different files provided. Two main datasets: 
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
bank_add <- read.csv("../Data/bank-additional-full.csv", sep = ";")
bank_full <- read.csv("../Data/bank-full.csv", sep = ";")
glimpse(bank_full)
```
`Bank-additional-full.csv` has `r dim(bank_full)[1]-dim(bank_add)[1]` fewer rows and additional columns: `r paste(setdiff(names(bank_add), names(bank_full)), collapse = ", ")`. 

Names only in `bank-full.csv`: `r paste(setdiff(names(bank_full), names(bank_add)), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r}
summary(bank_full %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)))
```

About `r scales::percent(mean(bank_full$y == "yes"), accuracy = 0.1)` of contacts in `bank-full.csv` subscribe. The rate by month is much higher in the months with fewer contacts. Bar labels are contact counts, and each month pools May 2008 through November 2010.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
month_levels <- c(
  "jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun",
  "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"
)

bank_full %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month_levels)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    contacts = n(),
    subscribe_rate = mean(y == "yes"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, subscribe_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(contacts)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Subscription rate by contact month",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Subscription rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Instead of using a `set.seed()` function, the authors provided samples for both datasets.

Remaining EDA should bring in the additional columns in `Bank-additional-full.csv` if macro economics seem appropriate. Macro is a would-be-nice in objective 1, and only if additional predictive power is found in objective 2.

Suspecting a seasonal trend.

## Numerical predictors

The numeric predictors in `bank-full.csv` are `age`, `balance`, `day`, `duration`, `campaign`, `pdays`, and `previous`. The scatterplot matrix uses those seven columns from `bank_full` (n = 45,211). Each upper-triangle entry is the Pearson correlation. Each diagonal panel is a kernel density. Each lower-triangle panel is the pairwise scatterplot.

`pdays` equal to −1 means the client was not previously contacted, so a Pearson correlation that includes `pdays` treats that code as a day count. The right tails of `balance`, `duration`, `campaign`, and `previous` set the axis ranges in the panels that use those predictors.

```{r ggpairs-numeric, fig.width=10, fig.height=10, message=FALSE}
library(GGally)

num_vars <- bank_full %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

ggpairs(
  bank_full,
  columns = num_vars,
  upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor", size = 3)),
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.05, size = 0.2)),
  diag = list(continuous = wrap("densityDiag", alpha = 0.4)),
  progress = FALSE
)
```

## Within-level subscription proportions

`bank-full.csv` supplies the counts below (n = 45,211). The first table is the marginal distribution of `y`. For a categorical predictor, `cnt` is the number of contacts at that level and that value of `y`, and `perc` equals `cnt` divided by the number of contacts in the level. Each bar shows `perc` for `y` equal to yes. `reorder()` places the highest within-level proportion at the left. The month chart above uses calendar order. The month bar in this section orders months by that proportion.

```{r}
bank_full %>%
  group_by(y) %>%
  summarise(cnt = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(perc = round(cnt / sum(cnt), 4))
```

```{r rate-bars, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, message=FALSE}
cat_vars <- bank_full %>%
  select(where(is.character), -y) %>%
  names()

for (var in cat_vars) {
  tab <- bank_full %>%
    group_by(.data[[var]], y) %>%
    summarise(cnt = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    mutate(perc = round(cnt / sum(cnt), 4)) %>%
    ungroup()

  print(tab)

  angle <- if (dplyr::n_distinct(tab[[var]]) > 4) 45 else 0

  p <- ggplot(
    filter(tab, y == "yes"),
    aes(
      x = reorder(.data[[var]], -perc),
      y = perc,
      colour = .data[[var]]
    )
  ) +
    geom_bar(
      aes(fill = .data[[var]]),
      stat = "identity",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Subscription proportion by", var),
      x = var,
      y = "Proportion subscribed"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = angle,
        hjust = if (angle > 0) 1 else 0.5
      )
    )

  print(p)
}
```
